audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and the full-layer phase sides read Skill/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Skill/Jayce/Jayce while every why says the opposite from level 3 onward.
audit.why: whys[2] through whys[5] all argue Gragas owns the lane once Drunken Rage and Body Slam are up and through his first item; only level 1 is cleanly yours and two items is even.
audit.corrected: Jayce, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level-6 phase text said 'Gragas's ultimate changes the math too' as boilerplate and never named the spike.
audit.why: Explosive Cask is a 100/85/70s displacement that can fling you into Body Slam range or under his tower; Jayce has no level-6 spike because his R is the stance-swap he already had.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is his spike, not a shared one.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five places credited Drunken Rage (W) with a heal ('empowered-auto heal').
audit.why: Riot's Drunken Rage text is damage reduction plus a bonus-magic-damage empowered auto — no healing. The sustain is Happy Hour (P), which heals periodically on ability use, so it is casts, not autos, that refill him.
audit.corrected: Damage reduction from Drunken Rage; healing from Happy Hour on every cast.

audit.why: Body Slam 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, Barrel Roll 10s at rank 1 and Drunken Rage's 5s are what decide when you may step to poke range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal line said only 'his healing fights your pattern'.
audit.why: The heal source is Happy Hour, which triggers per ability cast, so Grievous Wounds matters most during extended brawls rather than against autos.
audit.corrected: Names Happy Hour as the anti-heal target.

edits.before: Get Drunken Rage (W) up so its damage reduction and empowered-auto heal let him eat your gate-Q and brawl back
edits.after: Get Drunken Rage (W) up so its damage reduction and Happy Hour's per-cast heal let him eat your gate-Q and brawl

edits.before: He hits 2 and Drunken Rage (W) plus an empowered-auto heal start eating your poke, but he still can't punish you from range it's even.
edits.after: He hits 2 and Drunken Rage's damage reduction plus Happy Hour's per-cast heal start eating your poke, but he still can't punish you from range.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are your window: take Cannon Q and chip him with Shock Blast every time he walks up to a minion, because before he has Drunken Rage (W) his Barrel Roll poke costs him health and his empowered-auto heal isn't online to out-sustain it. Do NOT sit in melee form here. The catch is his level 3: once he has Barrel Roll, Drunken Rage damage reduction and Body Slam (E), he can tank your accelerated gate-Q and dash on top of you, and his empowered auto out-trades you if you brawl. Land your poke, then back off on your passive move speed before he closes.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are your window: take Cannon Q and chip him with Shock Blast every time he walks up to a minion, because before he has Drunken Rage (W) his Barrel Roll poke costs him health and Happy Hour only refills him when he actually casts. Do NOT sit in melee form here. The catch is his level 3: once he has Barrel Roll, Drunken Rage damage reduction and Body Slam (14s at rank 1), he can tank your accelerated gate-Q and dash on top of you, and his empowered auto out-trades you if you brawl. Land your poke, then back off on your passive move speed before he closes.

edits.before: This stays an even AP brawl, so it's a skill lane late. He builds tanky-AP (Riftmaker/Rylai) and his Drunken Rage damage reduction plus empowered-auto heal let him survive your single Cannon-Q-shred-Hammer burst and stat-check you, while his Cask zones your only escape. You keep relevance through poke: spread gate-Qs before fights, never get caught alone for a Cask pick, and use Thundering Blow's knockback to peel his Body Slam dive off you or your carry. Whoever lands their key cooldown first the gate-Q or the Cask wins the exchange.
edits.after: This stays an even AP brawl, so it's a skill lane late. He builds tanky-AP (Riftmaker/Rylai) and his Drunken Rage damage reduction plus Happy Hour's per-cast heal let him survive your single Cannon-Q-shred-Hammer burst and stat-check you, while his Cask zones your only escape. You keep relevance through poke: spread gate-Qs before fights, never get caught alone for a 70s Cask pick, and use Thundering Blow's knockback to peel his Body Slam dive off you or your carry. Whoever lands their key cooldown first the gate-Q or the Cask wins the exchange.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gragas must walk into your range.
edits.after: Barrel Roll, Drunken Rage and Body Slam are all online — he tanks the gate-Q and dashes on top of you to brawl back.

edits.before: Form-swapping IS the ult — six abilities against his four. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Your R is only the stance-swap you already had; Explosive Cask is a 100s fling into Body Slam range or under his tower.

edits.after: - Body Slam (E): 14s at rank 1, 12s at rank 5 — his only gap-close; step in the moment it is spent. - Barrel Roll: 10s at rank 1. - Drunken Rage: 5s. - Explosive Cask: 100s at rank 1.

edits.before: His engage. E-knock after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His only gap-close, 14s at rank 1. Step up the moment it is spent.

edits.before: The lane has chapters — the chart is the table of contents.
